description: A set of ordinances overhauling the French Labour Code, capping unfair-dismissal payouts, merging workplace employee bodies into a single 'comité social et économique', and giving more room to company-level bargaining.
significance: First major reform of Macron's presidency, aimed at making the labour market more flexible; strongly contested by unions.

law_name: Replacement of the wealth tax (ISF to IFI) and flat tax (PFU)
description: The 2018 budget replaced the broad wealth tax (ISF) with a narrower real-estate wealth tax (IFI) and introduced a 30% single flat-rate levy (prélèvement forfaitaire unique) on capital income.
significance: Emblematic and divisive pro-investment tax reform; critics dubbed Macron 'president of the rich', supporters cited capital attraction.

description: The 2018 'nouveau pacte ferroviaire' ended the special 'cheminot' employment status for new SNCF hires and opened the rail sector to competition, transforming SNCF into a joint-stock company.
significance: A landmark structural reform of a historic public enterprise, met with extended strikes.

law_name: PACTE law (Action Plan for Business Growth and Transformation)
description: A wide-ranging law simplifying rules for business creation and growth, easing thresholds, reforming employee savings, and enabling some privatisations.
significance: Flagship business-friendly reform of the first term.

law_name: Law reinforcing respect for the principles of the Republic ('séparatisme' law)
description: A law strengthening oversight of associations and places of worship, tightening rules on home schooling, and creating offences aimed at countering 'radical separatism' and protecting laïcité.
significance: Central to Macron's response to Islamist radicalisation; criticised by some as restricting civil liberties.

description: Reform raising the legal retirement age from 62 to 64 and accelerating the rise in required contribution years, adopted via Article 49.3 without a final Assembly vote.
significance: The most contested reform of the second term, triggering one of the longest recent protest movements; core provisions upheld by the Constitutional Council. (Overlaps with the polemics dataset.)

description: A law tightening immigration rules (residence, family reunification, asylum processing); parts were struck down by the Constitutional Council before promulgation.
significance: Highly contested; passed with votes from the far-right Rassemblement National, prompting debate within Macron's own camp.
